before: merge(left, right, by = "id") combines rows with equal id values. Its default is an inner join: unmatched keys are omitted. all.x = TRUE retains unmatched left rows with missing right-side values.

Repeated keys can create multiple row pairs: two matching left rows and two matching right rows produce four joined rows. Validate key uniqueness when your model expects one-to-one or many-to-one relationships. Do not silently interpret duplicated joins as new independent observations.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
left <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1), minutes = c(10, 20))
right <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1), label = c("a", "b"))
joined <- merge(left, right, by = "id")
cat(nrow(joined), "\n")
```
Expected output or behavior: 4. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

For this ID, each left row matches each right row.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```r
left <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1), minutes = c(10, 20))

joined <- merge(left, right, by = "id")
cat(nrow(joined), "\n")
```
The output is `4`. Two rows on each side give four pairs.
